answer: Each identity registers one meadow plot in the atlas folio, locks an 80-credit bond, and files a velvet sward transect for that plot serial. An auditor recomputes height from the atlas rainfall table, checks the transect against the serial, and burns the bond on a mismatch above 3 percent or a reused serial. The first filing costs 39 credits, the kth 39+5(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 2,536,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-sward ring fails because a rented transect carries another serial and the wrong rainfall expectation. An honest identity pays 39 once and recovers the bond after a clean check.
